source_text: Καὶ καθάπερ ὁ Γολιὰθ τῷ οἰκείῳ ξίφει τὴν κεφαλὴν ἀπετμήθη, οὕτω καὶ ὁ διάβολος θάνατον γεννήσας, διὰ θανάτου τροποῦται· καὶ τὴν εὐχερῆ μέθοδον τῆς οἰκείας ἀπάτης, ὄργανον ἰσχυρὸν τῆς ἰδίας ἀπωλείας εὑρίσκει· καθάπερ ἄγκιστρον περιπαρεὶς τῇ Θεότητι, καὶ τὸ σύνηθες δέλεαρ καταπιὼν ἀγρεύεται σαφῶς ὁ ἀγρεύειν οἰόμενος· καὶ Θεὸν ἀντὶ ἀνθρώπου κρατήσας. Διὰ τοῦτο μάρτυρες σκιρτῶσιν τὴν τοῦ δράκοντος κεφαλήν· καὶ πᾶν εἶδος βασάνων ὑπερορῶσιν. Ἀφ' οὗ γὰρ ὁ δεύτερος τὸν πρῶτον Ἀδὰμ ἐκ τοῦ πυθμένος τοῦ ᾅδου ὡς τὸν Ἰωνᾶν ἐκ τοῦ κήτους ἀνήγαγεν, καὶ τὸν ἀπατηθέντα, εἰς ἐντροπὴν τοῦ ἀπατήσαντος, οὐρανοπολίτην ἀνέδειξεν· ἐξ ἐκείνου πύλαι ᾅδου ἐκλείσθησαν· καὶ πύλαι οὐρανοῦ ἀνεῴχθησαν· ἀκώλυτον τοῖς μετὰ πίστεως ἀνιοῦσιν παραχωροῦσαι τὴν εἴσοδον. Πάλαι μὲν Ἰακὼβ κλίμακα ἐστηριγμένην ἕως τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐθεάσατο, καὶ τοὺς ἀγγέλους τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀναβαίνοντας καὶ καταβαίνοντας· νυνὶ δὲ διὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἄνθρωπος γενόμενος ὁ φιλάνθρωπος τὸν ἀπάνθρωπον λακτίσας τῷ ποδὶ τῆς θεότητος, καὶ τὸν ἄνθρωπον βαστάσας τῇ χειρὶ τῆς χριστότητος, τὸν ἄβατον αἰθέρα ποσὶν ἀνθρωπίνοις πεζεύσασθαι παρεσκεύασεν. Τότε οἱ ἄγγελοι ἀνέβαινον καὶ κατέβαινον· νυνὶ δὲ ὁ τῆς μεγάλης βουλῆς Ἄγγελος οὐκ ἀναβαίνει καὶ καταβαίνει· καὶ πόθεν γὰρ ποῦ μεταστήσεται ὁ πανταχοῦ παρών, καὶ τὰ πάντα πληρῶν, καὶ ἐν τῇ χειρὶ συνέχων τὰ [κόσμου] πέρατα; Ἅπαξ γὰρ κατέβη καὶ ἅπαξ ἀνέβη· οὐ μεταβάσει χρησάμενος φύσεως, ἀλλὰ συγκαταβάσει φιλανθρώπου χριστότητος· ὁ Λόγος τῷ Πατρὶ συγκαθήμενος, καὶ ὁ Λόγος ἐν τῇ μήτρᾳ αὐλιζόμενος, καὶ ὁ Λόγος πανταχοῦ εὑρισκόμενος, καὶ [τοῦ] τῶν ὅλων [Θεοῦ] μηδέποτε χωριζόμενος.
thought_title: The devil defeated by his own weapon and Christ's descent and ascent opening heaven
orientation: The preacher continues the argument by comparing the devil's defeat to Goliath's, explaining how Christ's descent to Hades and ascent opened heaven for believers, and contrasting the angels' movements on Jacob's ladder with the once-for-all descent and ascent of the Angel of Great Counsel.
pass_a_gloss: And just as Goliath was cut off with his own sword, so also the devil, having begotten death, is turned back through death; and he finds the easy method of his own deceit, a strong instrument of his own destruction; just as having hooked the Deity with a hook, and having swallowed the accustomed bait, the one thinking to hunt is clearly caught; and having prevailed against God instead of man. Because of this the martyrs leap upon the head of the dragon; and they look past every kind of torments. For from when the second Adam brought up the first Adam from the bottom of Hades as Jonah from the belly of the whale, and showed the deceived one a citizen of heaven for the shame of the deceiver; from that time the gates of Hades were shut; and the gates of heaven were opened; granting unobstructed entry to those ascending with faith. Long ago Jacob saw a ladder fixed as far as heaven, and the angels of God ascending and descending; but now, on account of the man, the philanthropic one having become man, having kicked the misanthrope with the foot of the Deity, and having lifted the man with the hand of the Christ-likeness, he prepared the untrodden ether to be walked on with human feet. Then the angels were ascending and descending; but now the Angel of the Great Counsel does not ascend and descend; for from where would he shift, he who is present everywhere, and fills all things, and holds the ends of the world in his hand? Once he descended and once he ascended; not using a change of nature, but by the condescension of philanthropic Christ-likeness; the Word sitting together with the Father, and the Word dwelling in the womb, and the Word being found everywhere, and never separated from the God of the whole.

lemmas.gloss: having hooked / caught with a hook

choices.why: The devil is portrayed as the father of death; 'begotten' preserves the generative metaphor.
In context the devil's own weapon (death) reverses on him; 'turned back' captures the reflexive defeat.
The verb means to catch with a hook; the image is the devil hooking the Deity as a fish.
Contrasts Adam (deceived) and the devil (deceiver) with parallel participles.
rejected: the one deceived ... the one deceiving

choices.why: Title for Christ emphasizing love for humanity; 'philanthropic' is the fixed glossary sense.
Preserves the wordplay: the second Adam (man) becomes man for the sake of the first man.
Contrast to philanthropic one; the devil as hater of humanity.

choices.english: the Angel of the Great Counsel
choices.why: Standard title for Christ from Isaiah 9:6 LXX; fixed in patristic usage.
rejected: the Messenger of the Great Plan

pass_b_english: Just as Goliath was beheaded with his own sword, so the devil, having begotten death, is turned back by means of death. He finds his easy method of deception, a strong instrument of his own ruin. Impaled on the Deity as on a fishhook, and swallowing the accustomed bait, the hunter is plainly caught. For he laid hold of God instead of a man. That is why the martyrs leap on the dragon's head and look past every kind of torture. For from the time the second Adam brought up the first Adam from the pit of Hades, as Jonah from the belly of the whale, and showed the deceived one to be a citizen of heaven for the shame of the deceiver, the gates of Hades have been shut and the gates of heaven have been opened, granting unimpeded entry to those who go up with faith. Long ago Jacob saw a ladder set firm up to heaven, with the angels of God ascending and descending on it. Now, because the philanthropic one became man for the sake of man, kicking the misanthrope with the foot of his divinity and bearing the man in the hand of his kindness, he has prepared the impassable ether to be walked on human feet. Then the angels went up and came down; but now the Angel of the Great Counsel does not go up and come down. For from where would he move, he who is present everywhere and fills all things and holds the ends of the world in his hand? Once he came down and once he went up, not by a change of nature but by the condescension of his loving kindness. The Word sits with the Father, and the Word dwells in the womb, and the Word is found everywhere, and never separated from the God of the whole.
notes: Bracketed words [κόσμου] and [τοῦ] [Θεοῦ] in the source indicate textual supplements; glossed as present.

problems.quote: He thought he had overcome God instead of a man.
problems.why: The source means he seized God when he expected a man. The English says he believed he had overcome God, which reverses the irony.
problems.fix: for he laid hold of God instead of a man.
problems.ruling: κρατήσας is having seized God; ἀντὶ ἀνθρώπου means not merely a man, not thought overcome God instead of man.

edits.old: He thought he had overcome God instead of a man.
edits.new: For he laid hold of God instead of a man.

fixed: Fixed overcoming-thought to seizing: κρατήσας means having seized/laid hold of, i.e. seized God (Θεὸν ἀντὶ ἀνθρώπου) when expecting a man.

problems.quote: He hooks the Deity as with a fishhook
problems.why: περιπαρείς is passive (impaled, pierced). The devil is caught on the Deity as on a hook; he does not hook the Deity.
problems.fix: Impaled on the Deity as on a fishhook,
problems.ruling: περιπαρείς passive: impaled on Θεότητι; English wrongly makes devil hook God

problems.quote: bearing the man in the hand of his christic power
problems.source_quote: τὸν ἄνθρωπον βαστάσας τῇ χειρὶ τῆς χριστότητος
problems.why: χριστότης means kindness or goodness, with a pun on Christ. It does not mean 'christic power'.
problems.fix: bearing man in the hand of his kindness
problems.ruling: χριστότητος is Christ-like kindness, not δύναμις; 'christic power' misleads

problems.quote: the condescension of philanthropic christic power
problems.why: χριστότης means goodness or kindness, not 'power'. The phrase speaks of his loving kindness stooping down.
problems.fix: the condescension of his loving kindness
problems.ruling: συγκαταβάσει φιλανθρώπου χριστότητος: condescension of kindness, not power

edits.old: He hooks the Deity as with a fishhook,
edits.new: Impaled on the Deity as on a fishhook,

edits.old: bearing the man in the hand of his christic power
edits.new: bearing the man in the hand of his kindness

edits.old: by the condescension of philanthropic christic power
edits.new: by the condescension of his loving kindness

fixed: agency: περιπαρεὶς is passive, devil impaled/caught on Deity, not hooking Deity
mistranslation: τῇ χειρὶ τῆς χριστότητος is kindness, not christic power
mistranslation: φιλανθρώπου χριστότητος is loving kindness, not christic power

last_rejected.quote: He finds his easy method of deception, a strong instrument of his own ruin.
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ τὴν εὐχερῆ μέθοδον τῆς οἰκείας ἀπάτης, ὄργανον ἰσχυρὸν τῆς ἰδίας ἀπωλείας εὑρίσκει
last_rejected.why: The Greek says his easy trick turns out to be what ruins him. The English reads as if he finds a way to deceive, which loses the reversal.
last_rejected.fix: His own easy method of deception he finds to be a strong instrument of his own ruin.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek apposes εὐχερῆ μέθοδον ἀπάτης with ὄργανον ἀπωλείας; English comma does the same—ruin is explicit, not a successful deceit.
